questions.heading: A Vertex Is Where Two Boundary Lines Cross Inside the Region
questions.stem: A region in (x, y) has the rows x >= 0, y >= 0, x <= 5, y <= 5 and x + y <= 8. The boundary lines x = 5 and y = 5 cross at (5, 5). Is (5, 5) a corner of the region?

options.text: Yes, because any two boundary lines that cross make a corner
options.says: A crossing is a corner only if every row allows it; some crossings lie outside the region.

options.text: No, because the point breaks x + y <= 8 and lies outside
options.says: Right: 5 + 5 = 10 > 8, so the crossing is infeasible and is not a vertex.

options.text: Yes, because both of its rows are tight at that point
options.says: Two tight rows make a crossing; it must also satisfy every other row to be a vertex.

options.text: No, because the lines x = 5 and y = 5 are parallel
options.says: The lines are perpendicular and do meet; the point fails a third row instead.

questions.heading: The Objective's Level Lines Are Parallel, and the Best Plan Is the Last Point the Line Touches
questions.stem: An LP maximizes 3x + 2y over a region whose corners are (0, 0), (0, 4), (3, 3) and (4, 0). Which plan is best?

options.text: (4, 0), since x earns more per unit than y does
options.says: A bigger coefficient does not decide it: (4, 0) is worth 12 and (3, 3) is worth 15, as with the budget split's corner B.

options.text: (0, 4), since y reaches its largest amount at that point
options.says: (0, 4) is worth only 8; the objective, not one variable's size, ranks plans.

options.text: (2, 2), since a middle plan balances the two limits
options.says: A level line cannot come to rest inside the region: from an inner point it can slide further.

options.text: (3, 3), since the level line touches the region last there
options.says: Right: 3x + 2y = 15 at (3, 3), more than at any other corner, so the sliding line stops there.

questions.heading: If an LP Has a Best Plan, Some Vertex Is a Best Plan
questions.stem: A maximization LP in two variables has corners A, B, C and D worth 40, 55, 55 and 30. B and C are neighbours, joined by one edge of the region. What can you say about the plans on that edge?

options.text: Every plan on the edge is optimal, each worth 55
options.says: Right: the level line for 55 runs along the edge, so every point on it reaches the best value.

options.text: Only B and C are optimal, since optima sit at corners
options.says: Some corner is always optimal, but with a tie the whole edge between the tied corners is optimal too.

options.text: The edge's midpoint is worth 110, since the two values add
options.says: A point on the edge is a weighted average of B and C, so its value is the average, 55.

options.text: The LP has no optimum, since the best plan is not unique
options.says: Several optimal plans is still an optimum; the solver returns one of them.
